subtopic: Journey versioning — structural edits require a new version; in-flight profiles stay on the old version
question: A welcome journey is live with 5,000 profiles in flight. The team needs to change a condition's logic and lengthen a wait activity — both structural changes. What must they do, and what happens to the in-flight profiles?

options.text: Edit the journey in place — live journeys accept structural edits, and in-flight profiles pick up the new logic at their next activity
Stop the live journey, edit the canvas, and republish — all 5,000 in-flight profiles are migrated onto the new canvas design
Create a new version; in-flight profiles finish on the old version and new entrants flow to the new version — but only when re-entrance is disabled
Create a new version from the latest version; in-flight profiles stay on the previous version until they exit, and new entries flow into the latest published version

why_correct: Structural changes to a live journey require creating a new version — only limited elements like name and message content can be edited while live. Publishing a new version does not move in-flight profiles: profiles that already entered a previous version stay in it until they exit the journey, while new entries flow into the latest published version. New versions can only be created from the latest version.

why_wrong.A: live journeys cannot be structurally edited in place; only name and message content are editable without a new version.
why_wrong.B: the documented path is a new version, not stop-and-edit, and publishing a new version never migrates in-flight profiles mid-flow.
why_wrong.C: version behavior has nothing to do with the re-entrance toggle; the cross-version rule is that a profile cannot be active in two versions at once — if still active in the old version, a new entry into the new version is blocked until the old instance ends.

subtopic: Channel capping rule sets — cross-channel counts and UTC-based resets
question: A marketer activates a channel rule set with one rule: at most 5 marketing messages per day, applied to the Email and SMS channels together. On Tuesday at 10:00 AM UTC, a profile has received 3 marketing emails and 2 marketing SMS. At 11:00 AM UTC a journey reaches an email send for that profile. What happens?

options.text: The email is sent — the rule counts 5 per channel, and the profile has only received 3 emails
The email is sent, and only then is the profile excluded from the rest of the day's sends
The profile is excluded from this delivery — the 5-message cap counts email and SMS together as a total, the profile already hit 5, and the daily counter resets at midnight UTC
The profile is excluded from all marketing sends for the rest of the week — daily caps roll up into a weekly lockout

why_correct: When several channels are selected in a capping rule, the capping count applies across all selected channels as a total — 3 emails + 2 SMS = 5, so the cap is hit and the profile is excluded from the very next delivery of any marketing email or SMS. Daily frequency caps are calendar-day based and reset to 0 at the start of the next day (midnight UTC).

why_wrong.A: treats the cap as per-channel; the documentation's example is explicit that multi-channel selection counts the total across channels.
why_wrong.B: the exclusion applies to the delivery that would exceed the cap, not the one after; the cap is already hit at 10:00 AM.
why_wrong.D: invents a weekly lockout; a daily rule resets daily with no roll-up.

subtopic: Custom action response handling — jo_status_code, timeout/error branch, errorResponse node
question: A journey calls a loyalty API through a newly created custom action. The endpoint returns HTTP 400, and the custom action has an error response payload defined. The marketer wants the journey to take a fallback path and branch on the specific error. How should they build this?

options.text: Put a condition in the success branch checking the response body — HTTP 400 responses still flow through the success path with an error flag

Enable the alternative timeout/error path and branch with @action{ActionLoyalty.jo_status_code} == "http_400" — a call is in error when the HTTP code is greater than 2xx, and the configured error response fields are exposed under the errorResponse node
Check jo_status_code in the success branch — jo_status_code only reports "timedout", and HTTP errors are invisible to the journey
Cache the response per journey run — Journey Optimizer calls the endpoint once per journey execution and reuses the payload for every profile

why_correct: An action call is considered in error when the returned HTTP code is greater than 2xx (or if an error occurs), and the journey flows to the dedicated timeout/error branch. The built-in jo_status_code field carries http_`<code>`/timedout/capped/internalError and can be used in a condition on that branch; when an error response payload is configured, its fields are exposed under the errorResponse node for failed calls.

why_wrong.A: HTTP codes above 2xx do not take the success path; they route to the timeout/error branch.
why_wrong.C: jo_status_code is not timeout-only; its values are http codes, timedout, capped, and internalError.
why_wrong.D: backwards: each profile entering the custom action triggers its own call — "even if the response is always the same, Journey will still perform one call per profile."

subtopic: Data view session settings — idle timeout and metric-based session start, applied at report time
question: An analyst wants every mobile app launch to start a new session AND wants sessions to expire after 30 minutes of inactivity. They make these changes in the data view today, then re-run a report covering last month. What happens?

options.text: Both changes apply immediately to the historical report — session timeout and the session-start metric are defined per data view, are non-destructive, and are applied at report time; other data views on the same connection are unaffected
The 30-minute timeout applies to the historical report, but the app-launch session start only applies to data collected after the change
The changes require a new connection — session settings are connection-level, not data-view-level
Sessions can only be defined by timeout, not by a metric — there is no way to start a new session on app launch in Customer Journey Analytics

why_correct: Session settings live in the data view (Settings tab): the session timeout (idle minutes/hours/days/weeks before a new session starts) and "Start new session with a metric" (e.g. a Launch metric built from an appInteraction schema field — the documentation's own example). Settings are non-destructive — multiple data views on one connection can each carry their own session definition — and, consistent with CJA's report-time processing, changes apply at report time to historical and future data alike without reprocessing.

why_wrong.B: describes Adobe Analytics behavior, where collection-time settings apply forward only; CJA inverts this.
why_wrong.C: session settings are data-view-level; the connection defines datasets, Person ID, retention, and backfill.
why_wrong.D: "Start new session with a metric" is an explicitly documented setting; the doc's example is literally the app-launch metric.

subtopic: Person ID and identity stitching in the connection — skipped rows, one-dataset stitching, case sensitivity
question: A connection joins a web event dataset (CRMid present on only 40% of rows, stitching not enabled) with a call-center dataset using CRMid as the Person ID. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The missing 60% are backfilled automatically — Customer Journey Analytics resolves missing Person IDs through the Device Co-op
Identity stitching merges the two datasets into a single stitched dataset before reporting
Person ID matching is case-insensitive, so "abc123" and "ABC123" join to the same person

Rows without a CRMid value are skipped from the connection's stitched data; enabling identity stitching (Select package or higher for field-based) rekeys rows within the web event dataset using authenticated and unauthenticated sessions to recover a common Person ID — stitching applies to that one dataset, not as a merge of the two

why_correct: "If a record doesn't contain a value for the identity you have selected as the Person ID for the event dataset, the record is skipped." Identity stitching rekeys identities within one dataset's rows — looking at both authenticated and unauthenticated sessions — to get the desired Person ID onto as many events as possible (where no common Person ID can be determined, the persistent ID value is used). Stitching is not a dataset merge: the datasets are combined by selecting the same person ID across them in the connection. Field-based stitching requires the Select package or higher; graph-based requires Prime or higher.

why_wrong.A: overclaims: CJA has no Device Co-op backfill for missing Person IDs (and stitching authenticated+unauthenticated data carries explicit consent/compliance prerequisites).
why_wrong.B: confuses stitching with merging; the docs state stitching applies to one dataset only.
why_wrong.C: Person ID values are case-sensitive: `abc123` and `ABC123` are treated as two different people.
